CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Eugene Walker is a 61-year-old male who presents today for routine follow-up. The patient has a significant cardiac history, having undergone aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013. He reports experiencing increased fatigue, which he attributes possibly to age. He remains active and continues to ride his road bike 20 to 30 miles, though he becomes tired afterward and requires rest; previously he could do 40 miles. His last stress test was performed on 9/9/2019. Being eight years post-op, he is concerned about the durability of his aortic valve and had requested an echocardiogram from Dr. Lewis. He denies any chest pain or acute cardiac symptoms. The patient reports that his wife and friends have noticed pursed lip breathing when he walks. He denies associated wheezing. He also reports a small nodule on his right epididymis that he incidentally discovered and wanted evaluated, though he is not overly concerned. He denies depression and describes himself as "a pretty happy guy overall." Sleep: 6 to 7 hours per night; works by 7am and attempts to work out in the mornings. He makes reservations twice weekly for a 5:45am swim. Wife reports he snores slightly but denies episodes of apnea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies wheezing, dyspnea, chest pain, apnea episodes, or depression. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair (1/22/2013).

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3: 50,000 units on Sundays, 2,000 units on other six days.
Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a lecturer. He is married. He cycles regularly on a road bike (20-30 miles typically). He swims twice weekly at 5:45am. He attempts morning workouts. He does not regularly follow up at Hopkins due to stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing, doing well overall.
Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing observed, low exhalation phase, clear to auscultation, no wheezing.
Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3mm palpable nodule not felt to be epididymis or varicocele; left testicle normal; no hernia.
All other portions of physical exam: Normal.

Total cholesterol: 247 (elevated)
HDL: 66

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient is doing well overall and currently asymptomatic. Not currently followed by cardiology. Will order echocardiogram and stress test. Referral to Dr. Vincent Sanchez in cardiology recommended for ongoing management.

2. Elevated alkaline phosphatase: Most recent labs showed elevation at 156, likely related to bone health but could be related to liver function. Will recheck alkaline phosphatase and GGT today. Results will be sent through patient portal unless abnormal, in which case patient will be called.

3. Abnormal lung findings/Pursed lip breathing: Patient reports increased fatigue with exertion but remains active with biking 20-30 miles. Pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase noted on examination. Will order pulmonary function tests for further evaluation.

4. Right testicular nodule: 2-3mm palpable nodule noted on examination. Referral to urology placed for possible ultrasound evaluation.

5. Preventative health: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended and will be scheduled for next month. COVID-19 vaccination series complete (doses on 1/15/2021 and 2/5/2021).

6. Follow-up: Patient to return in one year for wellness visit, sooner if needed after review of all laboratory studies and imaging. Patient instructed to call with any questions or concerns.
